🪪 Upload Identity Document Drag and drop your Passport, Driver's License, or State ID. We will automatically extract your demographics and taxpayer data.
OR MANUAL ENTRY
⚠️
Dual Residency Conflict Detected You are classified as a tax resident under both US domestic laws (Calendar Year: Jan–Dec) and Indian domestic laws (Fiscal Year: Apr–Mar). This creates overlapping worldwide tax exposure.
DTAA Article 4 Tie-Breaker

Under the India-US Treaty, you can resolve dual residency by breaking the tie to one country using these sequential tests: Permanent Home ➔ Center of Vital Interests ➔ Habitual Abode ➔ Nationality. Breaking the tie to India allows you to file in the US as a Non-Resident Alien (Form 1040-NR + Form 8833).

Tax Year Mismatch & FTC Apportionment

If you do not break the tie, you must claim a Foreign Tax Credit (FTC Form 1116) to avoid double taxation. Because the Indian Fiscal Year (April–March) crosses two US Calendar Years, it is highly recommended to claim FTC on an accrued basis and file for a US tax extension (Form 4868) to file by Oct 15, allowing the Indian tax liability to finalize.

Article 4 Tie-Breaker Wizard

Corporate Residency Determination

Unlike individuals, corporate tax residency is not based on days spent in the US. It is determined purely by the jurisdiction of incorporation or organization.

Incorporated / Organized in the United States? Yes = Domestic entity. No = Foreign entity with different filing obligations.
Domestic Entity

This entity is subject to US tax on its worldwide income under the applicable form (1120 / 1120-S / 1065 / 1041).

Foreign Entity

This entity is only subject to US tax on US-source income (ECI / FDAP). Additional foreign reporting may apply.

Are you a US Citizen? Worldwide taxing rights regardless of stay.
Hold a US Green Card? Form I-551 creates tax residency.
§877A Covered Expatriate Tests

A Long-Term Resident (green card held 8+ of the last 15 years) who surrenders it is a "covered expatriate" — subject to §877A mark-to-market exit tax — if ANY ONE of the three tests below is met.

Test 1: covered expatriate if ≥ $2,000,000 (fixed, not inflation-adjusted).
Test 2: covered expatriate if > $211,000 (2026, inflation-adjusted under Rev. Proc. 2025-32).
Form 8854: Can you certify 5 years of federal tax compliance? Test 3: failure to certify (or leaving this unchecked) makes you a covered expatriate regardless of net worth or tax liability.
Sets Residency Starting Date for standard dual-status. Worldwide taxation begins here.
Sets Residency Termination Date. Worldwide taxation ends here.

To meet the Substantial Presence Test, you must be physically present in the U.S. for at least 31 days during the current year, and the weighted sum of days over the 3-year period must be at least 183 days.

Closer Connection Claim? Form 8840 (Active if stays < 183 days)
Enter the year you first arrived in the U.S. on this visa (e.g., 2022). Even a single day counts as a full year.
Total number of calendar years (before 2026) that you spent any part of in the U.S. on this visa.
Extend Student Tax-Exempt Status (Over 5 Years) Check this box if you have been in the U.S. for more than 5 calendar years but want to continue excluding your days. You must not plan to reside permanently in the U.S., must have a closer connection to your home country, and must file Form 8843.
Extend Scholar Tax-Exempt Status (Over 2 Years) Check this box if you have been in the U.S. as a scholar/teacher for more than 2 calendar years but qualify for an exemption extension under lookback rules (e.g., if you had no U.S. tax presence in the last 6 years).
First-Year Choice Election (§7701(b)(4)) Arrived mid-year and don't meet the SPT yet? Elect to pull your residency start date forward to this year — you remain a dual-status alien (nonresident before, resident from that date), not a full-year resident.
Your U.S. residency is counted from this date onwards for this year.
Non-Resident Spouse Joint Filing Election Elect to treat a Non-Resident Alien spouse as a US Resident to unlock Married Filing Jointly (MFJ) for the full year.
📋
First-Year Election Active — Key Consequences By turning this on, you remain a dual-status alien for this year — nonresident (US-source income only) before your entry date, resident (worldwide income) from that date onward. This is a formal IRS election with significant implications, including losing the standard deduction for the year.
What This Election Does

Without this election, an arrival that doesn't meet the SPT until next year is a Non-Resident Alien for all of this year. This election pulls your residency starting date forward to the first day of the qualifying 31-day period — you become a dual-status alien: Non-Resident Alien (US-source income only) before that date, Resident Alien (worldwide income) from that date through Dec 31. It does NOT make you a full-year resident — for that, a married couple needs the separate §6013(g)/(h) election below.

IRS Eligibility Conditions

To qualify, you must: (1) not have been a U.S. resident in the prior year, (2) be present in the U.S. for at least 31 consecutive days during this year, and (3) be present for at least 75% of the days from your first day of arrival to December 31. If these are not met, the election is invalid.

🔍 Nexus of Life — Audit Defence

When you leave a high-tax state, auditors look beyond your lease date — they check where your family actually lives. Answer these to make your domicile change defensible.

Active-duty military member or military spouse? Under the Military Spouses Residency Relief Act (MSRRA), you can keep your home-state residency regardless of where your orders station you — this may eliminate state tax in your duty-station state.
ℹ️ MSRRA Tax Protection Active: Your service-connected wages and spouse wages are exempt from taxation in your duty-station state. They are only taxable in your legal home state of record. Ensure you file form DD 2058 and state-specific military withholding exemption certificates (e.g. Form DE-4 for CA, Form IT-2104-MS for NY).
California FTB — Domicile & Exit Planning

California aggressively audits departing residents. The Franchise Tax Board looks at every tie you keep after you leave.

Are you planning to leave California? Triggers the CA domicile-exit planning workflow.
Do you still own CA property or hold CA voter registration? Strong sign the FTB will contest your non-residency.
⚠️ FTB Exit Checklist Activated: Domicile exit requires severing CA ties. Ensure you: (1) close CA bank accounts, (2) move primary bank accounts/brokerages, (3) cancel CA voter registration, and (4) surrender CA driver's license/DMV registration.
⚠️ High Audit Risk: Retaining California residential real property, active California voter registration, or a California driver's license are primary indicators of ongoing California domicile. The FTB routinely wins audits on departing residents who maintain these ties.
Domicile / Incorporation State

Physical Presence Nexus

Select states where your business has physical assets, inventory, offices, or W-2 employees (including remote workers working from their homes). Physical presence almost always triggers state income/franchise tax.

Economic Nexus (Sales Thresholds)

Even without physical presence, exceeding sales thresholds (usually $100k or 200 transactions) in a state creates Economic Nexus for Sales Tax and increasingly for Income Tax.

Multi-State Apportionment
Does the entity operate in multiple states? Requires calculating sales, property, and payroll factors to apportion income.

                QBI & SSTB Tax Guide
            
    
            
        
    
        
        
        
    
            
            
        
    

        
        
    
            
            
            
    
                
    
                    
    What is the Section 199A QBI Deduction?
    
                    
    It allows self-employed individuals and owners of pass-through businesses (sole proprietorships, partnerships, S-corps, and trusts) to deduct up to 20% of their net business income from their personal income tax.
    
                
    

                
    
                    
    Core Eligibility Checklist
    
                    
      
                        
    • 
                            ✓
                            
      
                                Active U.S. Business:
                                Must be a domestic U.S. trade or business operations (Schedule C, Schedule F, or K-1 pass-throughs).
                            
      
                        
      • 
                        
    • 
                            ✓
                            
      
                                Positive Net Profit:
                                Calculated on the net business profit. If the business has a net loss, QBI is $0 (and is suspended/carried forward).
                            
      
                        
      • 
                        
    • 
                            ✕
                            
      
                                Not W-2 Employment:
                                Performing services as a W-2 employee is strictly ineligible.
                            
      
                        
      • 
                    
    
                
    

                
    
                    
    Standard Eligible Business Examples
    
                    
    
                        
    
                            Trades & General Operations:
                            • Retail Stores & E-Commerce
    
                            • Restaurants, Cafes & Food Services
    
                            • Manufacturing & Wholesaling
    
                            • Construction Contractors & Builders
    
                            • Real Estate Agents & Landlords (Active)
    
                            • Farms & Ranches (Schedule F)
                        
    
                        
    
                            Exempt Professional Services:
                            • Architects & Designers
    
                            • Engineering Firms & Inspectors
    
                            • Salons, Barber Shops & Personal Care
    
                            • Dry Cleaning, Garages & Repair Shops
    
                            • Tourism & Logistics Companies
                        
    
                    
    
                
    

                
    
                    ⚠️ Income Threshold Alert
                    
    For high-income taxpayers (above $201,775 Single / $403,500 Joint in 2026), the QBI deduction is restricted or completely phased out if the business is a Specified Service Trade or Business (SSTB) or fails standard W-2 wage / UBIA property cap limits. Review the next tab to check if your business is an SSTB.
    
                
    
            
    

            
            
    
                
    
                    
    What is a Specified Service Trade or Business (SSTB)?
    
                    
    An SSTB is any business where the principal asset is the reputation or skill of one or more of its owners or employees. If your business is an SSTB, your QBI deduction is phased down above the lower limit and **completely eliminated** above the upper limit.
    
                
    

                
    
                    
    Exhaustive SSTB Categories (IRS §199A)
    
                    
    
                        
    
                            
    
                                1. Health Services
                                Doctors, nurses, dentists, veterinarians, physical therapists, psychiatrists, etc.
                            
    
                            
    
                                2. Law Firms
                                Attorneys, paralegals, legal consultants, arbitrators.
                            
    
                            
    
                                3. Accounting
                                CPAs, enrolled agents, bookkeepers, tax preparers.
                            
    
                            
    
                                4. Consulting
                                Business consulting, strategic planning, lobbyists, policy advisors.
                            
    
                            
    
                                5. Performing Arts
                                Actors, singers, musicians, entertainers, stage directors.
                            
    
                        
    
                        
    
                            
    
                                6. Athletics
                                Professional athletes, coaches, trainers, sports managers.
                            
    
                            
    
                                7. Financial & Brokerage Services
                                Investment bankers, portfolio managers, stockbrokers, trading consultants.
                            
    
                            
    
                                8. Investing & Trading
                                Dealing or trading in securities, commodities, or partnership interests.
                            
    
                            
    
                                9. Reputation & Skill
                                Receiving fees/royalties for endorsement, appearances, or licensing of name/image/voice.
                            
    
                        
    
                    
    
                
    

                
    
                    📌 Rule of Thumb for Checklist Settings
                    • Income Below $201,775 (Single) / $403,500 (MFJ): You can select QBI Eligible regardless of whether your business is an SSTB.
    
                    • Income Above $251,775 (Single) / $503,500 (MFJ): If your business falls under any SSTB category above, you **must NOT** check the QBI Eligible box (or if selected, the engine will disallow the deduction automatically).
